items.title: Lifecycle identity is named without a complete state machine
items.statement: The window requires spawning on first file open using host, server, and root identity, but does not define deduplication under concurrent opens, behavior when a root changes, shutdown after the last file closes, replacement of stale instances, or consumers responsible for each transition.
items.impact: Duplicate or orphaned servers can consume resources, race requests, or attach diagnostics to the wrong workspace.
items.builder_discretion: Specify an authoritative per-identity state machine, atomic spawn ownership, reference counting or equivalent liveness rule, and terminal cleanup semantics.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Phase 2 server lifecycle spawns on first file open by host/server/root identity, restarts on crash with backoff, supports stdio-to-TCP bridge commands such as Godot, and documents the bridge pattern.

items.title: Crash backoff and bridge recovery are not bounded
items.statement: Restart-on-crash is required, but the window does not define backoff schedule, jitter, retry ceiling, healthy-reset rule, cancellation, crash-loop terminal state, pending-request disposition, or cleanup and reconnection when either side of the stdio-to-TCP bridge fails.
items.impact: A crash loop or half-open bridge can create resource storms, hung requests, or silently stale language intelligence.
items.builder_discretion: Define bounded retries, cancellation and cleanup, request failure semantics, health reset, and an observable degraded or terminal state.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Phase 2 server lifecycle spawns on first file open by host/server/root identity, restarts on crash with backoff, supports stdio-to-TCP bridge commands such as Godot, and documents the bridge pattern.

items.title: Custom bridge commands and TCP endpoints lack a trust boundary
items.statement: The bridge requirement permits custom commands and TCP transport without specifying who may configure or execute a command, executable and argument validation, environment inheritance, endpoint allowlisting, authentication, workspace trust, or whether traffic may leave the local machine.
items.impact: Untrusted workspace configuration could execute arbitrary programs or expose source and diagnostics over an unintended network endpoint.
items.builder_discretion: Define configuration authority, workspace-trust and approval policy, command and endpoint validation, local-only defaults, secret handling, and transport security.

items.title: Phase 3 units do not encode their Phase 2 prerequisites
items.statement: Assistant diagnostics and Chat navigation depend operationally on an available LSP lifecycle, yet the accepted Phase 3 units declare no dependencies or unblocks. The window therefore does not prevent an invalid compile or rollout order.
items.impact: Phase 3 surfaces may be considered ready while the server lifecycle and bridge needed to supply them are absent or unstable.
items.builder_discretion: Encode prerequisite PlanUnits and readiness conditions for Phase 3 consumers.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Chat LSP phase 3 includes current LSP diagnostics in Assistant and Interview context with file, line, message, severity, and source for project, at-mentioned, or recently edited files.

items.title: Assistant diagnostic context has no scope, retention, or freshness policy
items.statement: Project, at-mentioned, and recently edited diagnostics are eligible for Assistant or Interview context, but the window does not define workspace isolation, selection precedence, recency interval, maximum volume, stale-version handling, user visibility or opt-out, redaction, or retention after the turn.
items.impact: Sensitive paths and messages may cross workspace or conversational boundaries, stale diagnostics may mislead the model, and large projects may overload context.
items.builder_discretion: Define a bounded, versioned, user-inspectable selection policy with workspace isolation, redaction, expiration, and retention rules.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Chat LSP phase 3 includes current LSP diagnostics in Assistant and Interview context with file, line, message, severity, and source for project, at-mentioned, or recently edited files.

items.title: Diagnostic text is not classified as untrusted model input
items.statement: File names, messages, and diagnostic sources can be controlled by project content or third-party language servers, but the window does not require delimiting, escaping, provenance tagging, or instruction-isolation before injecting them into Assistant or Interview context.
items.impact: Adversarial diagnostics can become prompt-injection material or cause the assistant to treat untrusted text as instructions.
items.builder_discretion: Treat all LSP payload text as untrusted data, preserve provenance, delimit it structurally, and prohibit it from acquiring instruction authority.

items.title: Chat navigation does not define stale-target or URI-mapping behavior
items.statement: Hover and click-to-definition may use virtual documents or real file URIs, but the window does not define document lifetime, version mapping, language identity, unsaved-buffer mapping, permission checks, behavior after edits, or what the user sees when the target is stale, missing, or outside the workspace.
items.impact: A click can open the wrong location, expose an unauthorized path, or appear successful while navigating against obsolete content.
items.builder_discretion: Specify versioned virtual-document mapping, URI authorization, capability checks, stale-target detection, and explicit failure feedback.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Chat phase 3 uses LSP workspace/symbol for @ symbol results and supports hover and click-to-definition in chat code blocks through virtual documents or real file URIs.

items.title: LSP-unavailable fallback can silently misrepresent capability and completeness
items.statement: The fallback omits diagnostics and disables hover or definition, but the window does not require an availability indicator, distinguish total from per-server or per-file failure, define reconnect and refresh behavior, or prevent a Problems count from being presented as complete during degradation.
items.impact: Users may interpret absent diagnostics as a clean project or assume navigation is broken without knowing the LSP is unavailable.
items.builder_discretion: Expose scoped availability and staleness, distinguish partial outages, disable or qualify affected controls, and refresh deterministically after recovery.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Chat phase 3 exposes Problems links or badges and optional compact diagnostics hints for at-mentioned files, while fallback uses text/indexed symbol search, no hover/definition, and omitted diagnostics when LSP is unavailable.

items.title: Optional Phase 4 readiness and deferral states are not operationalized
items.statement: The phase may add features as optional or explicitly deferred, but the window does not define who chooses each state, where the state is recorded, readiness prerequisites, compatibility behavior when disabled, or how operators and users distinguish deferred from unavailable or failed.
items.impact: Implementations can diverge on whether a capability is required, disabled, unsupported, or broken, weakening rollout and support truth.
items.builder_discretion: Define authoritative feature states, decision ownership, readiness gates, and observable disabled, deferred, unavailable, and failed presentations.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Optional phase 4 may add an LSP diagnostics gate, LSP evidence snapshots, and subagent selection bias from LSP diagnostics as optional or explicitly deferred enhancements.

items.title: Diagnostics gates and evidence snapshots lack deterministic or privacy-safe oracles
items.statement: The window names an optional no-error gate and evidence snapshot without defining diagnostic stabilization, severity and scope filtering, server disagreement, timeout and crash handling, reproducibility, snapshot schema, path and message redaction, retention, or what makes gate evidence pass or fail.
items.impact: The same source state can produce inconsistent gate results, while evidence artifacts may persist sensitive paths or diagnostic text.
items.builder_discretion: Define a versioned snapshot contract, quiescence and timeout rules, severity and scope policy, failure classifications, redaction, retention, and deterministic pass or fail oracle.

items.title: Mutating quick actions lack preview, atomicity, and rollback contracts
items.statement: Fix all and format file can rewrite broad content, while rename can span files. Aside from rename confirmation, the window does not specify preview, affected-file disclosure, authority boundaries, version conflict detection, atomic application, partial-edit recovery, undo, cancellation, or concurrent edit handling.
items.impact: A quick action can silently overwrite user changes or leave a partially transformed repository after an error or race.
items.builder_discretion: Require scoped previews and approvals proportional to impact, version preconditions, transactional or compensating behavior, cancellation, and durable undo or recovery receipts.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Optional chat enhancements may expose Fix all, LSP rename with confirmation, where-used references, format file, and copying hover type/signature to Chat.

items.title: Chat rename explicitly requires confirmation
items.statement: The quick-action requirement explicitly preserves confirmation for LSP rename, so the basic user-consent requirement for that named Chat action is not missing, although preview, scope, rollback, and stale-version semantics remain gaps.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Optional chat enhancements may expose Fix all, LSP rename with confirmation, where-used references, format file, and copying hover type/signature to Chat.

items.title: Tool promotion and experimental-flag migration have no readiness contract
items.statement: The window permits removing or relaxing OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_LSP_TOOL only when ready, but does not define readiness evidence, capability negotiation, version compatibility, persisted-setting migration, rollback, staged rollout, or behavior for clients and servers that support only a subset of the promoted methods.
items.impact: Promotion can expose unsupported tools, break existing opt-in behavior, or make rollback impossible after clients persist the new default.
items.builder_discretion: Define capability and version gates, migration and rollback semantics, staged rollout evidence, and subset-support behavior before changing the experimental flag.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Optional tool promotion may expose lsp.references, lsp.definition, lsp.hover, and approval-gated lsp.rename and remove or relax OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_LSP_TOOL only when ready.

items.title: Promoted lsp.rename remains approval gated
items.statement: The tool-promotion unit contains an explicit negative constraint that lsp.rename remains user-approval gated if promoted. This closes the basic authority question for invocation approval, without closing edit-scope, preview, race, or rollback questions.

evidence.exact_quote: - lsp.rename remains user-approval gated if promoted.

items.title: Acceptance and validation surfaces do not test runtime behavior
items.statement: Across the reviewed units, acceptance is framed as source preservation, addressability, metadata traceability, and prohibition of WorkNode creation, while validation invokes migration and index validators. No executable oracle in this window falsifies lifecycle, navigation, fallback, safety, privacy, or recovery behavior.
items.impact: Plan governance can pass while every user-visible and failure-mode contract in the window remains unimplemented or incorrect.
items.builder_discretion: Add behavior-level acceptance oracles for each runtime and GUI contract, including negative, failure, race, recovery, permission, accessibility, and migration cases.

evidence.exact_quote: - The covered source span remains losslessly available for exact-text audit.

items.title: Chat links, badges, hints, and modified-click navigation lack accessibility contracts
items.statement: The window names Problems links or badges, compact hints, click-through, and Ctrl+Click, but does not define keyboard-only equivalents independent of a pointer modifier, focus order, accessible names and roles, live announcement of counts or availability changes, contrast, or non-color severity cues.
items.impact: Keyboard, screen-reader, low-vision, or motor-impaired users may be unable to discover state or invoke equivalent navigation.
items.builder_discretion: Specify semantic roles and names, complete keyboard operation, focus behavior, announcements, contrast, and non-color state cues with accessibility tests.

items.title: User-visible diagnostic summaries lack localization rules
items.statement: The Problems count and compact error hint are preserved as user-visible concepts, but the window does not define pluralization, number formatting, message truncation, bidirectional-path handling, locale switching, or treatment of language-server messages that are not in the UI locale.
items.impact: Counts and diagnostics may be grammatically wrong, unreadable, clipped, or directionally confusing in supported locales.
items.builder_discretion: Use localized parameterized messages with plural rules and bidirectional isolation, and define truncation plus raw-message locale behavior.

items.title: Owner boundary points to unnamed SSOT consumers and empty ContractRefs
items.statement: Each unit says referenced owner documents retain SSOT boundaries, yet this window names only LSPSupport as an owner hint and preserves no ContractRefs. The actual owners and consumers for Chat, Assistant, Interview, Problems, tools, evidence, settings, and lifecycle operations are therefore not traceably identified here.
items.impact: Required behavior can be duplicated, omitted, or implemented inconsistently because downstream owners cannot be derived from the unit metadata.
items.builder_discretion: Add concrete owner references and ContractRefs for every cross-surface consumer, with one adjudicated SSOT for each shared behavior.

evidence.exact_quote: - Plans/LSPSupport.md owns LSP-specific protocol/client constraints while referenced owner docs retain their SSOT boundaries.

items.title: Lifecycle, bridge, and context behavior lack support observability
items.statement: The window does not define structured events, health state, retry and crash-loop metrics, bridge endpoint status, request correlation, diagnostic-context provenance, support-safe logs, or user-facing diagnostics for the lifecycle and Chat integrations.
items.impact: Operators and users cannot distinguish server crashes, bridge loss, capability absence, stale data, fallback activation, or policy rejection without unsafe raw logs.
items.builder_discretion: Define privacy-safe structured telemetry, correlation, health and degradation states, support export, and user-facing diagnostics for each failure boundary.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Phase 2 server lifecycle spawns on first file open by host/server/root identity, restarts on crash with backoff, supports stdio-to-TCP bridge commands such as Godot, and documents the bridge pattern.

items.title: Network loss and reconnection semantics are absent
items.statement: The reviewed behavior includes a TCP bridge and an LSP-unavailable fallback, but does not define connect timeout, mid-request disconnect, reconnection ownership and backoff, queued request handling, cached or stale result policy, transition out of fallback, or behavior when only one server loses connectivity.
items.impact: Requests can hang or replay, stale UI can survive reconnection, and recovered capability can remain silently disabled or duplicate operations.
items.builder_discretion: Specify connection states, bounded timeouts and reconnects, request idempotency and failure rules, cache staleness, and deterministic fallback-to-live transition.

items.title: Direct Chat interaction units are classified as GUI-related
items.statement: The units governing click-to-definition and Problems links or badges are explicitly marked gui_related true, so their user-visible nature is not lost in classification even though their detailed GUI truth and accessibility contracts remain incomplete.

items.title: Referenced owner documents may contain missing contracts but are not identifiable in this window
items.statement: The owner-boundary note asserts that referenced owner documents retain SSOT boundaries, but no referenced documents or ContractRefs are present in the reviewed core. Under blind-window constraints it is therefore unknown whether another owner already defines the missing security, privacy, GUI, recovery, migration, and test contracts.
items.impact: This review can establish that the assigned window is incomplete but cannot safely claim repository-wide absence or duplication.
items.builder_discretion: Resolve the named owner references during the cross-document phase and then classify each window-level gap as externally satisfied, duplicated, conflicting, or still open.

evidence.exact_quote: - Plans/LSPSupport.md owns LSP-specific protocol/client constraints while referenced owner docs retain their SSOT boundaries.

dimension_assessments.summary: Lifecycle transition owners and downstream Chat, Assistant, Interview, Problems, tool, evidence, and support consumers are not fully identified.
Lifecycle, phase ordering, fallback, recovery, and optional-feature states lack complete transitions and invariants.
Concurrent opens, crashes, reconnects, edits, and workspace-wide mutations have no atomic ownership or stale-version rules.
Half-open bridges, per-server outages, stale targets, and multi-file edit failure are not specified.
Crash-loop recovery, bridge cleanup, fallback exit, and rollback or undo for mutations are absent.
Custom command, endpoint, diagnostic-context, feature-state, and broad-edit authority are underdefined; rename invocation approval is an explicit non-gap.
Bridge traffic, diagnostic context, copied signatures, and evidence snapshots lack isolation, redaction, retention, and disposal rules.
Workspace-configured bridge commands and language-server diagnostic payloads are not constrained or treated as untrusted data.
Navigation and Problems surfaces do not fully disclose stale targets, partial outages, omitted diagnostics, or fallback state; GUI classification itself is preserved.
TCP disconnect, timeouts, reconnection, request replay, cache staleness, and deterministic exit from fallback are unspecified.
Server-instance growth, restart storms, project-wide diagnostics volume, symbol result size, and broad-edit fan-out have no limits or backpressure.
Links, badges, hints, counts, and modified-click navigation lack keyboard, semantic, focus, announcement, and visual accessibility contracts.
Counts, compact hints, raw diagnostics, paths, and copied signatures lack pluralization, formatting, directionality, and locale behavior.
URI mapping, capability subsets, protocol and platform variation, and experimental-flag migration or rollback are not defined.
Runtime health, crash loops, bridge state, fallback activation, diagnostic provenance, and support-safe evidence are not observable by contract.
Fix all, format, and rename lack complete preview, scope, conflict, atomicity, and undo semantics; both rename surfaces explicitly preserve approval or confirmation.
Phase dependencies and named owner or consumer references are absent despite repeated statements that other owner documents retain SSOT boundaries.
Metadata validators do not falsify runtime behavior, and the optional diagnostics gate lacks deterministic pass or fail semantics.
The blind window cannot establish whether unnamed referenced owner documents already satisfy, duplicate, or conflict with the identified missing contracts.
